__doc__: A DELIBERATELY WRONG DCGM contract, for the negative case in
compose/gpu-metrics-sim.py --selftest.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A checker that only ever runs against the real contract
is a checker nobody has watched fail. It can rot into one that accepts
anything — an over-broad match, a `problems` list that is built and never
returned, an exception swallowed into a pass — and the real run cannot reveal
that, because a checker that accepts everything also accepts the truth.
So the selftest feeds this file and asserts the checker REJECTS it. Proving it
by hand-editing tests/contracts/dcgm-surface.json and reverting does not count:
nothing enforces the revert, and the next person finds a contract that has
quietly been wrong since whenever the experiment was abandoned.
It is wrong in three independent ways, one per direction the checker has to
detect, so a rejection cannot come from whichever single case happens to be
implemented:
1. DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE is MISSING     -> the producer emits a series the
contract does not list
2. DCGM_FI_DEV_SM_CLOCK is ADDED      -> the contract lists a series the
producer does not emit. Chosen on
purpose: SM_CLOCK is the series the
fake exporter genuinely cannot emit,
so this is the shape a real mistake
would take.
3. modelName is spelled model_name    -> a label-key rename, the drift that
blanks a dashboard legend without
blanking the panel
Never point the compose simulator or verify.sh at this file.
